entry.summary:
What is IAM?
IAM (Identity and Access Management) is the heart of AWS security. It decides: Who can access our AWS account What they can do (read, write, delete, launch etc.) Which services/resources they can interact with IAM helps us securely control access without sharing our Root account (super admin--my free tier root user acc). A User = one person with credentials (username + password or access key). Created by the Root user (owner of AWS account). We give only the permissions they need, nothing more! entry.title: EA's latest The Sims 4 patch is making everyone pregnant, including the men and the chaste
entry.summary: EA’s latest Sims 4 patch—dropped alongside the Enchanted by Nature expansion—has unleashed a wild pregnancy bug: Sims of every gender, age and relationship status (yes, even men, kids and total virgins) are suddenly expecting. Once knocked up, they stop aging, can’t Woo-Hoo or blow out birthday candles, and there’s no in-game test to prove it’s a glitch rather than a miracle. Unsurprisingly, players are losing it over this unintentional baby boom. Fingers crossed EA rolls out a fix (and a “remove baby” spell) ASAP before your entire town becomes a maternity ward.

Sure, it’s doing fine on the sales charts, but it’s not dragging old Guardians back or convincing new recruits to stick around. The real problem? None of the big issues are fixed. entry.title: Oblivion Remastered studio is reportedly laying off 300 people
entry.summary: Virtuos—the co-development whiz behind Oblivion Remastered, Dark Souls Remastered and the upcoming Metal Gear Solid Δ—has reportedly laid off about 300 staff (roughly 7% of its workforce). The news comes via French games journalist Gauthier “Gautoz” Andres on Bluesky, who points out that even working on one of the biggest hits of 2025 didn’t spare teams from cuts. Apparently, Virtuos’ “over-quality” approach on a fixed‐fee, no‐royalty contract meant blockbuster success didn’t translate into bonuses. So despite helping churn out some of the year’s best-selling titles, a chunk of the studio is now waiting for the axe to drop—and it’s a harsh reminder that even big hits don’t always pay off for the folks doing the heavy lifting.

entry.title: Subnautica 2 Devs Sue Publisher Krafton Which Has Accused Them Of Abandoning The Project
entry.summary: Subnautica 2’s sequel hit choppy waters when Unknown Worlds’ top trio—CEO Ted Gill and co-founders Charlie Cleveland and Max McGuire—jumped ship after Krafton announced a 2026 delay. The ex-devs are now suing Krafton for breach of contract, alleging the push-back was a sneaky way to dodge a $250 million bonus they’d share with the team. Krafton fired back, calling their departure a betrayal and claiming leadership bailed to chase side projects, which they say caused content cuts and schedule chaos. Amid leaked internal slides and public press releases, Krafton insists the delay was purely to polish the game (not mess with bonuses) and has tapped Steve Papoutsis as the new CEO to keep things afloat. With both sides trading accusations—“confusion in direction” vs. “financial gamesmanship”—fans are left waiting to see who sinks first in this high-stakes legal standoff.
